newsitem.title: LEBANON: Solidere end week down on oversupply.
newsitem.headline: Solidere end week down on oversupply.

text.p: Solidere shares fell on the Beirut Stock Exchange in the week ended on Friday and dealers said oversupply resulted in the drop.
A shares fell to $110 from $111.875 last Friday and B shares also dropped to $114 from $115.875.
Turnover in Solidere shares was 31,089 shares from last week's 34,852 and value was $3,514,404 against $3,962,037.

"Solidere is pulling out. There is a lot of supply and very little demand. Prices of A shares could have fallen further on Friday had it not been to some kind of interference on the market", a dealer who wished not to be identified said.
He said a block of demand orders pushed prices up on the second fixing. A shares closed at $108.375 on the first fixing at 0800 gmt.
A total of 16,500 shares of Ciments Libanais were traded on the BSE during the week. The shares closed at $1.156 from $1.21875 on December 5 when they had last been traded.
A block of 70,000 shares were traded over the counter at $1.20.
Also traded on the BSE were 3,000 shares of piping maker Eternit unchanged at $1.75.
There was no trade in the shares of Ciments Blancs and Uniceramic.
The LISPI stock index fell 1.22 percent on the week to 81.20 and the BLOM stock index also fell 2.18 percent to 937.75.
